page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Marginal notes in the left margin only: a date-like number at the level of the Vandal war passage, a number at the level of the Sforza passage, and a multi-line italic side note beside the paragraph starting "His". Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: manicus sanguis mifceatur: quin etiam Ducem Saxo-nicum admissurum dedecus, si cum isto cane ( sic enim Mistivojum appellare solebat ) affinitate devinceretur. Mistivojus hac contumelia irritatus, illico abnegata fide Christiana totam Vandalicam gentem ad arma excitavit: missoque feciali ad Theodoricum, nunciare illi jussit: Mistivojum, canem istum Vandalicum, jamjam editurum latratum, effecturumq; morsus, quos tota Marchia & Saxonia perhorrescat. Cum autem Theodoricus non minus ferociter respondisset, Se curaturum ca-nicidas, qui latratum & rabiem ejus compescant: 1520[?]& non exspectato auxilio, cum Vandalis temere conflixisset: mox victus & profligatus, totaque sua ditione exutus; quoad vixit, nulla unquam aut reconciliatione potiri, aut suam ditionem a Vandalis recuperare potuit: nec amicorum quemquam habuit, a quo restitueretur: sed omnibus invisus, in perpetuo exilio vitam traduxit miseram: Magdeburgi eleemosyna Canonicorum sustentatus: ut in ejus vita scribit Georgius Sabinus.

Hujusmodi tragicum eventum & exitum habuit quoque LUDOVICUS SFORCIA Mediolanensium Princeps, teste Gvicciardino lib.4. hist. Italicæ: qui nimia arrogantia & fastu, se arbitrum totius Italiæ fore putaverat: & tamen inter Helvetios milites, domum discedentes, amictu gregarii militis latitans, a Gallis agnitus & ignominiosè captus; Lugduni clatrato in 1508[?]carcere decem circiter annos captivus, mortalium omnium miserrimus periit.

Princeps ad humilitatem erga Deum, & modestia se excitet:His & similibus exemplis prudens Princeps admonitus de rerum omnium instabilitate: si qua in re numen maxime favens atque propitium habet; in ea fortunæ beneficia prudenter dispensare, iisque sapienter uti meminerit: & consideratione humanæ fragilitatis atque imbecillitatis, & simul fortunæ lubricitatis atque inconstantiæ, semetipsum ad humilitatem & modestiam excitet: exemplo NABUCHODONOSORIS: qui ob nimium fastum e regno ejectus, postquam in solitudi-

page.notes: Left margin marks read as "1520" beside the Vandal passage and "1508" beside the Sforza passage; both uncertain. The side note beside "His" is italic and set in the margin. Long s was normalised to plain s throughout, and double "ff" (printed for ss) was written as "ss". Ligature "ft" was read as "st". The line break "ca-nicidas" is a printed hyphen. The text ends with "solitudi-" and the catchword "ne va-" lies at the bottom right, as printed.
